messages.content: [lab-A] Fictional record for Ada Example: creatinine 1.2 mg/dL, specimen serum, 2026-09-01. Extract analyte, value, unit and evidence ID. Do not infer a diagnosis.

[note-A] This fictional encounter belongs to patient P-102, not P-101. The earlier draft used P-101 by mistake. [lab-B] Potassium 4.1 mmol/L. Correct the patient label and report the lab result with its evidence ID.
[visit-A] Fictional visit, 2026-08-01: heart rate 88 beats/min. [visit-B] 2026-08-03: heart rate 76 beats/min. Build a two-entry timeline with dates, values, units and evidence IDs.
[med-A] Fictional record: medication X, dose 5 mg, route oral. Frequency is absent. Extract the documented fields and explicitly identify the missing frequency. Do not choose a schedule.
Medication X, 5 mg, oral; frequency is missing. [med-A]
[assay-A] Fictional cell assay: control fluorescence 120 AU, treated fluorescence 84 AU. Report the treated/control ratio, retaining original observations and citation. Do not infer efficacy.
Control 120 AU; treated 84 AU; treated/control ratio 0.70. [assay-A]
[run-A] Fictional sequencing QC: sample S1 has 240 reads and 180 pass QC; sample S2 has 200 reads and 100 pass QC. Report each pass fraction as a percentage and cite the run.
[experiment-A] Fictional protein assay has technical replicates 0.20, 0.21 and 0.19 absorbance units from one biological sample. State the number of technical replicates and biological samples.
Three technical replicates from one biological sample. [experiment-A]

[study-A] Fictional study A reports increased marker abundance after treatment. [study-B] Fictional study B reports no change under a different sampling protocol. Summarize both and preserve the disagreement; do not claim a consensus.
Study A reports increased marker abundance [study-A]; study B reports no change [study-B]. The results differ and used different sampling protocols.
